Order filled. Here's the summary.

**Summary:** I researched Apple's most recent reported results using primary sources and then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a $223.00 limit (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 total, against a last price of $222.70 — inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, with the $50,000 cash balance untouched otherwise and no money moved out). The case for buying: Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth quarter (ended Sept 28, 2024) revenue was $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, reversing the prior year's revenue decline, and full-year FY2024 total net sales were $391,035 million versus $383,285 million in FY2023, with operating income of $123,216 million — evidence that the core franchise is expanding again. FY2024 net income of $93,736 million and diluted EPS of $6.08 were both depressed by a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge, so underlying profitability is meaningfully better than the reported year-over-year EPS dip ($6.08 vs. $6.13) implies, which is why I read the print as modestly positive rather than deteriorating. I deliberately ignored a promotional-looking "StreetTicker" item about a "QNTX" stock surging on an "Apple contract," which was quarantined by the security screen and is not corroborated by any Apple or SEC filing, and I based the decision only on the Apple newsroom release and the FY2024 Form 10-K.
